name: Ensuring Proper Window Flashing and Waterproofing in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How can Los Angeles County homeowners verify that a window installer will properly flash and waterproof openings for heavy winter rains, not just rely on caulking?
mainEntity.text: How can Los Angeles County homeowners verify that a window installer will properly flash and waterproof openings for heavy winter rains, not just rely on caulking?

acceptedAnswer.text: Water intrusion around poorly installed windows is a major issue in many Los Angeles County homes, especially during heavy winter storms. Caulking alone is not a reliable long-term defense. Before hiring an installer, ask them to walk you through their waterproofing sequence: removal of old materials, preparation of the rough opening, pan flashing at the sill, self-adhesive or membrane flashing on jambs and head, and integration with housewrap or stucco paper. Request written installation specifications or a simple diagram showing how they layer flashing and where they terminate it. A professional company should be able to provide manufacturer installation instructions that align with industry standards. Ask specifically whether they install a sill pan or equivalent system to prevent water from pooling at the bottom of the window frame. You can also ask to see jobsite photos from past projects, looking for visible membrane flashing, metal head flashing, and careful integration with building paper before the final stucco or trim goes on. During your own project, be present on the first day or two and politely request to see one opening before it is closed up. Installers who are confident in their waterproofing practices are usually willing to explain and show their methods.
acceptedAnswer.description: To verify proper waterproofing, Los Angeles County homeowners should ask installers to describe their flashing system, request written specifications or diagrams, confirm use of pan flashing, self-adhesive membranes, and head flashing, and ask for photos of past installations that show more than surface caulking.
